sub_agendas_items.title: Planning, Building and Development Services Department - Transportation Master Plan – Rural Lens – Verbal Update
sub_agendas_items.minutes:
At the outset, Vice-Chair C. Kelly introduced the following Motion to allow for the Committee’s receipt of this item at the meeting:
Motion No. ARAC 2025 25-01
Moved by Vice-Chair C. Kelly:
BE IT RESOLVED THAT the Agriculture and Rural Affairs Committee approve that the Rules of Procedure be waived subject to Subsection 83(4) of the Procedure By-Law (being By-Law No. 2025-100) to receive a staff presentation / update on the Transportation Master Plan – Rural Lens.
Carried
The Committee then received a verbal update from Mr. Max Walker, Senior Project Manager, Transportation Planning, Planning, Development and Building Services Department (PDBS), Ms Deborah Lightman, Program Manager,Transportation Policy and Networks, PDBS and Ms Jennifer Armstrong, Director, Transportation Planning, PDBS.  A copy of the slide presentation they spoke to is held on file with the Office of the City Clerk.
The Committee heard from Ms Leeanne Van der Burgt, President, Manotick Village and Community Association, who shared a brief video with the Committee, a copy of which is held on file with the City Clerk.
Following questions to the presenter and to staff, and at the conclusion of Committee discussions, the Chair introduced the following Direction to Staff:
Direction to staff (Councillor D. Brown)
Transportation Master Plan (TMP) Active Transportation Project - Feasibility study
The 2023 Transportation Master Plan (TMP) Active Transportation Project list includes a feasibility study to provide active transportation facilities on Manotick Main Street between Eastman Avenue and Century Road East. As part of the recently released draft 2025 TMP Capital Infrastructure Plan, this feasibility study is identified as a first phase priority.  In the next few years, there is also an upcoming resurfacing project for Manotick Main Street which offers potential coordination opportunities.    
Given the above considerations, staff are directed to initiate work on the feasibility study for Manotick Main Street as soon as possible after Council’s approval of the Capital Infrastructure Plan and project priorities in July 2025, and as part of the study, staff consult with community stakeholders and residents, and identify opportunities to coordinate with the planned resurfacing project.
Staff indicated that they would accept the above as Direction.  The Committee then ‘Received’ the presentation for information.

sub_agendas_items.description:
File No. ACS2025-OCC-CCS-0071 - West Carleton-March (5)
This item was referred from Council on May 28, 2025 as per CC Motion No. 21D.

motions.motion_text:
Report Recommendation(s)
That the Agriculture and Rural Affairs Committee consider the matter for recommendation to Council.
At the outset, Ms Debbie Stewart, General Manager, Strategic Initiatives (SI) Department, spoke to provide context on this item.
In addition to the General Manager, the following members of staff were also present to respond to questions:
Vice-Chair Kelly then read out the following Motion:

WHEREAS as part of the proposed South March battery energy storage system (BESS) project at 2555 and 2625 Marchurst Road, the proponent has publicly stated that it plans to establish a “Community Development Fund” of $250,000 per year to support local projects; and
WHEREAS the City of Ottawa has previously entered into host municipality responsibility agreements with third-party project proponents who provide funds related to community initiatives in recognition of the project’s effects on the local community; and
WHEREAS host municipality responsibility agreements generally provide for the City to determine how to allocate and disburse funds provided by the third party in order to respond to community needs and ensure accountability and transparency, with eligible community initiatives often identified by City staff in consultation with the relevant Ward Councillor(s);
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that staff,in the event this project proceeds,be directed to request that the South March BESS project proponent fulfill its stated intent to establish a “Community Development Fund” by entering into a host municipality responsibility agreement with the City of Ottawa through which the proponent would provide an amount of at least $250,000 per year with the goal to achieve a higher amount if possible, for a period of not less than 20 years. The finalization and execution of such agreement shall be approved by Council, with recommendations to be provided as to the allocation and disbursements of such funds;
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that staff be directed to provide City Council with an update on the status of the request to the proponent by way of memorandum within three months of the approval of a Municipal Support Resolution for the South March BESS project, and to bring forward for committee and Council approval any draft host municipality responsibility agreement negotiated with the proponent.
Committee then heard from the following public delegations:
The following spoke in support of the MSR for the South March BESS Project:
The following spoke in opposition to theMSR for the South March BESS Project:
Correspondence was also received from the following, in opposition to the MSR for the South March BESS Project (unless noted otherwise):
[ Individuals / groups marked with an asterisk (*) provided written submissions.  Individuals marked with a cross (+) provided a slide presentation.  Individuals marked with a ‘vee’ (v) provided a video presentation.  ALL are held on file with the Office of the City Clerk. ]
As the hour was approaching 7:00 p.m., the following Motion was considered:

BE IT RESOLVED that the Agriculture and Rural Affairs Committee meeting time be extended past 7:00 p.m. pursuant to Subsection 8(1)(c) ofProcedure By-law(By-law No. 2025-100).
Following the receipt of all public delegations, questions to the presenters and to staff, and at the conclusion of Committee deliberations, the following Motions were introduced and considered as noted:

(as amended from the original, introduced earlier in the meeting)
WHEREAS as part of the proposed South March battery energy storage system (BESS) project at 2555 and 2625 Marchurst Road, the proponent has publicly stated that it plans to establish a “Community Development Fund” of $250,000 per year to support local projects; and
WHEREAS the City of Ottawa has previously entered into host municipality responsibility agreements with third-party project proponents who provide funds related to community initiatives in recognition of the project’s effects on the local community; and
WHEREAS host municipality responsibility agreements generally provide for the City to determine how to allocate and disburse funds provided by the third party in order to respond to community needs and ensure accountability and transparency, with eligible community initiatives often identified by City staff in consultation with the relevant Ward Councillor(s);
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that staff,in the event this project proceeds,be directed to request that the South March BESS project proponent fulfill its stated intent to establish a “Community Development Fund” by entering into a host municipality responsibility agreement with the City of Ottawa through which the proponent would provide an amount of at least $250,000 per year with the goal to achieve a higher amount if possible, for a period of not less than 20 years. The finalization and execution of such agreement shall be approved by Council, with recommendations to be provided as to the allocation and disbursements of such funds;
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that staff be directed to provide City Council with an update on the status of the request to the proponent by way of memorandum within three months of the approval of a Municipal Support Resolution for the South March BESS project, and to bring forward for committee and Council approval any draft host municipality responsibility agreement negotiated with the proponent.
The above motion was put to a vote and was ‘Carried’ as noted below:

WHEREAS at its meeting of May 28, 2025 Council directed that the Agriculture and Rural Affairs Committee provide a recommendation for the June 11, 2025 meeting of Council to either accept or deny a Municipal Support Resolution for the South March BESS project; and
WHEREAS the Agriculture and Rural Affairs Committee heard from a number of delegations at its meeting of June 5, 2025 and considered the request for a Municipal Support Resolution;
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that the Agriculture and Rural Affairs Committee recommend Council deny the request for a Municipal Support Resolution for the South March BESS project.
The above motion was put to a vote and was ‘Carried’ as noted below:
That the Agriculture and Rural Affairs Committee recommend Council:
